long_biography.plain_text:
Andrew Colin put his own capital behind a university-partnership model that combined teaching with international recruitment. At INTO, investment in overseas marketing was accompanied by separate property companies that developed centres and leased their buildings to universities. The academic institutions retained responsibility for standards while sharing ownership of the ventures.

Through INTO Giving, Colin supported educational projects with matching donations. His contributions were reserved for new initiatives, while the company helped cover the charity's running costs. The charity also organised regular sponsorship of vulnerable schoolchildren in Zambia, funded by donations from staff and students.
